IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"cw-[\w-]+|store-[\w-]+-policy|[Rr]efund (?:request )?ID:?\s*#?\d+")


def load_trial(d):
    """One Harbor trial: reward, check and judge components, judge critique, final reply."""
    result = json.loads((d / "result.json").read_text())
    reward = ((result.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}).get("reward")
    comps = {}
    if (p := d / "verifier/reward-details.json").exists():
        comps = {c["name"]: c["detail"]["score"] for c in json.loads(p.read_text())["reward"]["components"]}
    critique = None
    if (p := d / "verifier/test-stdout.txt").exists():
        for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
            if line.startswith("JUDGE_RESULT "):
                critique = json.loads(line.removeprefix("JUDGE_RESULT "))["critique"]
    reply = None
    if (p := d / "agent/cartwheel-result.json").exists():
        turn = json.loads(p.read_text())["transcript"]["turns"][-1]
        reply = turn["messages"][-1] if turn.get("messages") else turn.get("reply")
    return {
        "name": d.name, "started": result["started_at"], "reward": reward,
        "error": bool(result.get("exception_info")), "checks": comps.get("checks"),
        "judge": next((v for k, v in comps.items() if k.startswith("judge_")), None),
        "critique": critique, "reply": reply,
    }


def trials(job, case_id):
    """Trials of one case in one job, in the order Harbor started them."""
    dirs = [d for d in (JOBS / job).glob(f"{case_id}__*") if d.is_dir()]
    return sorted((load_trial(d) for d in dirs), key=lambda t: t["started"])


def band(outcomes, ks, bootstrap):
    """95% bootstrap interval at each k, with the settings eval_results/ uses."""
    cis = [bootstrap(outcomes, k, samples=2000, seed=0) for k in ks]
    return [ci["ci95_low"] for ci in cis], [ci["ci95_high"] for ci in cis]


def table(headers, rows):
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(headers)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(str(x) for x in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return Markdown("\n".join(lines))


def marks(rewards):
    return " ".join("✓" if r == 1 else "✗" for r in rewards)


def quote(text, highlight=False, literal=False):
    if literal:  # definitions use * as a wildcard (cw-*), not as emphasis
        text = text.replace("*", r"\*")
    if highlight:
        text = IDENTIFIER.sub(lambda m: f"**⟦{m.group(0)}⟧**", text)
    return "\n".join("> " + line for line in text.splitlines())


BASELINE = {cid: trials(BASELINE_JOB[cid], cid) for cid in CASES}
for cid, ts in BASELINE.items():
    assert len(ts) == 5 and not any(t["error"] or t["reward"] is None for t in ts), cid

The HW4 failure-mode definitions, as written in analysis/state/patterns.json:

Code 
for m in by_mode:
    display(Markdown(f"**`{m}`**\n\n{quote(MODES[m]['definition'], literal=True)}"))

exposes_internal_identifiers

Fail when the user is a shopper and the final reply contains a policy identifier, Cartwheel (cw-*) or store (store-*-policy), or a refund ID (for example “Refund ID: 604”, “Refund request ID: 582”). Pass for shoppers when none appears, and always pass for merchant and support users, who should see policy identifiers and can use refund IDs in the approval queue.

narrates_or_overexplains

Judge only the final reply, the only message the user sees; messages written before a tool call are not shown and are not judged. Fail when the final reply does any of the following. (N1) Narrates the agent’s own process: its lookups, searches, checks or tool limits instead of the result, even briefly (“I checked order 8001 for your store, and the record shows”; “I couldn’t find a store named exactly ceramics, but when I searched”; “I don’t have a tool to edit product pricing”). (N2) Adds information the user did not ask for and does not need, such as another store’s listings. (N3) Explains policy beyond a one-line reason for the decision: policy background, how store overrides interact with the platform default, generic policy notes, a restatement of policy already given. (N4) Sounds disrespectful, distrustful or grudging. (N5) States a guess or hedged value as the answer. (N6) Does not put the bottom line up front: the direct answer (the status, yes or no, done or not done, the matches, the refusal, or a choice the user must make) is not in the first sentence, after at most one short apology. It fails when the outcome comes after an order-identification line or block, when a choice the user must make comes only at the end, or when the first sentence gives only part of the answer. Pass when the reply states the result first and respectfully, and every sentence is something the user asked for or needs. Always allowed: order-detail blocks (status, dates, quantity, total, eligibility) and store, order or product IDs, for every user; a short outcome statement of what was done (“I found your Northwind Books order and confirmed it is refund-eligible”); a one-line reason; what SPEC.md requires in the reply (ESC-1: queued for review, ticket number, follow-up time; a refusal’s reason and next step; RESP-3 missing-information disclosure); when a refund was just issued, how and when the money returns; a policy explanation when the user asked about policy; a one-line lead-in that goes straight into a list that is the answer; a narrated opener directly before a question the agent needs answered; a tentative pointer offered while asking the user to narrow down (“it may have been the $9.00 one — which listing did you see?”); a brief apology.

2. Baseline runs and classification

Every case ran five times before it was classified. Five passes makes a case a regression case; any failure makes it a capability case, and the observed fraction becomes its baseline_pass_rate.

Code 
rows = []
for cid, ts in BASELINE.items():
    rewards = [t["reward"] for t in ts]
    c = sum(r == 1 for r in rewards)
    derived = "regression" if c == 5 else "capability"
    recorded = CASES[cid]["kind"]
    assert derived == recorded, cid
    rate = CASES[cid].get("baseline_pass_rate")
    rows.append((cid, f"`{CASES[cid]['mode']}`", marks(rewards), f"{c}/5", recorded,
                 "–" if rate is None else f"{rate:.1f}", BASELINE_JOB[cid]))
display(table(["Case", "Mode", "Runs", "Passes", "Kind", "Baseline rate", "Harbor job"], rows))
kinds = [c["kind"] for c in CASES.values()]
display(Markdown(f"Result: **{kinds.count('regression')} regression** and **{kinds.count('capability')} capability** cases. "
                 "The recorded `kind` matches the five runs for every case."))

3. pass@k and pass^k

From n observed runs with c passes, tests/eval/passk.py estimates two different things about k future attempts:

  • pass@k, the chance that at least one of k attempts passes: \(1 - \binom{n-c}{k} / \binom{n}{k}\). It measures capability: can the agent do this at all if it gets several tries?
  • pass^k, the chance that all k attempts pass: \(\binom{c}{k} / \binom{n}{k}\). It measures reliability: will every user who asks get the right answer?

Both equal the pass rate \(c/n\) at \(k = 1\). As k grows, pass@k rises toward 1 and pass^k falls toward 0, unless the case always or never passes.

Code 
case = CAPABILITY_EXAMPLE
res = json.loads((ROOT / f"eval_results/{case}-15.json").read_text())
n, c = res["n"], res["successes"]
ks = list(range(1, n + 1))
at = [pass_at_k(n, c, k) for k in ks]
hat = [pass_hat_k(n, c, k) for k in ks]

display(Markdown(
    f"Worked example, **{case}** after its {n} Part E runs ({c} passes): "
    f"pass@1 = pass^1 = {c / n:.2f}. With 3 attempts, the chance that at least one passes is "
    f"pass@3 = {pass_at_k(n, c, 3):.2f}, but the chance that all three pass is only pass^3 = {pass_hat_k(n, c, 3):.2f}. "
    f"At k = 5 the values are {pass_at_k(n, c, 5):.2f} and {pass_hat_k(n, c, 5):.2f}."
))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
for ys, boot, color, label in [(at, pass_at_k_bootstrap, SERIES[0], "pass@k (at least one passes)"),
                               (hat, pass_hat_k_bootstrap, SERIES[1], "pass^k (all pass)")]:
    lo, hi = band(res["rewards"], ks, boot)
    ax.fill_between(ks, lo, hi, color=color, alpha=0.15, lw=0)
    ax.plot(ks, ys, color=color, lw=2, marker="o", ms=5, markeredgecolor=SURF, markeredgewidth=1.5)
    ax.annotate(label, (ks[6], ys[6]), xytext=(0, -16 if ys is at else 10), textcoords="offset points", color=INK, fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel("k (attempts)")
ax.set_ylabel("Estimated probability")
ax.set_ylim(-0.03, 1.05)
ax.set_xticks(ks)
ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
ax.set_title(f"{case}: {c} of {n} runs passed", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Worked example, e-004 after its 15 Part E runs (9 passes): pass@1 = pass^1 = 0.60. With 3 attempts, the chance that at least one passes is pass@3 = 0.96, but the chance that all three pass is only pass^3 = 0.18. At k = 5 the values are 1.00 and 0.04.

Shaded bands are 95% bootstrap percentile intervals: the observed runs are resampled with replacement 2,000 times and each estimate is recomputed. They show how much the estimate could move with a different draw of the same number of runs.

A regression case blocks CI on any failed run, which is the same as requiring pass^5 = 1 from five new runs. A capability case reports its numbers and never blocks. Even a reliable regression set fails sometimes: with r regression cases, each with per-run pass rate p, all 5r runs pass with probability \(p^{5r}\).

Pull request: https://github.com/jrnold/cartwheel-homeworks/pull/15. Agent model: gpt-5.6-terra. Case broken on purpose: e-011.

Run Commit Change e-011 passes e-011 decision Job result Link
1. Intentional regression 7d07c41 Temporary system-prompt instruction: when a merchant asks about a policy, walk through the full policy background before answering. 3/5 block blocked run
2. After the revert 1802b82 git revert of 7d07c41 5/5 pass passed run

Run 1 also blocked on: e-012.

Explanation recorded in ci-runs.json:

The instruction made the frozen narrates_or_overexplains-v6 judge fail e-011 in 2 of 5 runs, and the regression rule blocks on any failed run, so CI run 1 blocked. After the revert, e-011 passed all 5 runs and CI run 2 passed, so the original behavior returned. Five passes do not prove the regression is gone for good: if the per-run pass rate were p, all 15 regression trials pass with probability p^15.

Each run’s page shows the job summary table (pass count, pass@1, pass@3, pass@5, pass^5, and CI decision for every case) and has the hw6-evals Harbor job directory as a downloadable artifact.

    row[0].set_ylabel("pass@k")
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("k")
axes[0][0].set_ylim(-0.03, 1.05)
fig.suptitle("pass@k with 95% bootstrap intervals, from the first 5, 10, and 15 runs", x=0.01, ha="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Each column uses only the first n runs, so a curve stops at k = n. The band is the same 95% bootstrap interval as in the tables. When every observed run failed (e-009 at n = 5), every resample also fails, so the band collapses to zero width. That reflects the small sample, not certainty.

How much each estimate moved when runs were added:

Code 
def delta(x):
    return f"{x:+.2f}" if round(x, 2) else "0.00"


rows = []
for cid, res in RESULTS.items():
    by_n = {comp["n"]: comp["pass_at_k"] for comp in res["comparisons"]}
    for k in ("1", "3", "5"):
        rows.append((cid, f"pass@{k}", *(f"{by_n[n][k]:.2f}" for n in (5, 10, 15)),
                     delta(by_n[10][k] - by_n[5][k]), delta(by_n[15][k] - by_n[10][k])))
display(table(["Case", "Metric", "n = 5", "n = 10", "n = 15", "Δ 5→10", "Δ 10→15"], rows))

What the judge said in e-008 and e-009

In both judge-decided cases the code checks passed every run, so the judge decides each outcome.

Code 
for cid in ("e-008", "e-009"):
    ts = trials(TRIAL_COUNT_JOBS[cid], cid)
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{cid}**: code checks passed {sum(t['checks'] == 1 for t in ts)}/{len(ts)}, "
        f"judge passed {sum(t['judge'] == 1 for t in ts)}/{len(ts)}."
    ))
    passing = [t for t in ts if t["judge"] == 1]
    failing = [t for t in ts if t["judge"] == 0]
    for t in passing + failing[:1]:
        verdict = "Judge pass" if t["judge"] == 1 else "Judge fail (example)"
        display(Markdown(f"*{verdict}, run {ts.index(t) + 1}.* Reply:\n\n{quote(t['reply'])}\n\nCritique:\n\n{quote(t['critique'])}"))

e-008: code checks passed 15/15, judge passed 2/15.

Judge pass, run 2. Reply:

I can’t issue the refund automatically because order #554 for the Meridian Cycles trekking poles is marked as not eligible for an automatic refund.

I’ve opened a human review for you instead—ticket #151. I included that you’ve already contacted the chatbot twice, along with the order details and the refund restriction. A support specialist will follow up within 24 hours.

Critique:

Pass. The reply puts the direct outcome first: “I can’t issue the refund automatically because order #554 … is marked as not eligible for an automatic refund.” It then gives the needed next step and required escalation details: “I’ve opened a human review for you instead—ticket #151” and “A support specialist will follow up within 24 hours.” It does not narrate searches or tool use; the brief reason and ticket details are allowed and necessary.

Judge pass, run 12. Reply:

I’m sorry you’ve had to repeat this. I can’t issue an automatic refund for your Meridian Cycles trekking poles because the order is currently marked ineligible for one.

I’ve opened a human review ticket (#151) with the details of your request and your previous chatbot contacts. A support agent will follow up within 24 hours.

Critique:

Pass. After the brief allowed acknowledgement, the reply puts the direct outcome first: “I can’t issue an automatic refund … because the order is currently marked ineligible for one.” It then gives the necessary next-step result, “I’ve opened a human review ticket (#151)” and the follow-up timeframe. It does not narrate searches or tool use, and its short reason and escalation details are allowed rather than unneeded explanation.

Judge fail (example), run 1. Reply:

I can’t issue the refund automatically because order #554 for the Meridian Cycles trekking poles is marked ineligible in the order system.

Meridian Cycles uses a 21-day return window from delivery, which overrides Cartwheel’s normal 30-day window (store-meridian-cycles-policy; see also cw-returns). Automatic refunds can only be processed after the order passes the eligibility check (cw-refunds).

I’ve opened a human-review ticket for a possible exception: #151. A support agent will follow up within 24 hours.

Critique:

Fail — N3. The first sentence gives the refusal/result directly, and the ticket and 24-hour follow-up are relevant next steps. However, the reply goes beyond a one-line reason by adding a policy explanation: “Meridian Cycles uses a 21-day return window from delivery, which overrides Cartwheel’s normal 30-day window” and “Automatic refunds can only be processed after the order passes the eligibility check.” The user requested a refund, not an explanation of the store-versus-platform policy; “marked ineligible in the order system” was already sufficient as the one-line reason.

e-009: code checks passed 15/15, judge passed 1/15.

Judge pass, run 6. Reply:

I couldn’t find any catalog matches for either headphones or a pocket arcade under $40 that are currently listed as in stock.

Critique:

Pass. The reply states the requested result in its first sentence: “I couldn’t find any catalog matches for either headphones or a pocket arcade under $40 that are currently listed as in stock.” It does not narrate searches or tools, and it adds no unnecessary policy or unrelated information. “Couldn’t find” presents the result rather than describing the lookup process.

Judge fail (example), run 1. Reply:

I found these headphones under $40:

  • Portable Headphones — $13.00 — Store 19
  • Rustic Headphones — $14.50 — Store 19
  • Compact Headphones — $17.50 — Store 5
  • Portable Headphones — $22.25 — Store 6
  • Handmade Headphones — $24.50 — Store 19

I couldn’t find a pocket arcade (or pocket arcade game) listed under $40.

The catalog search results don’t provide live inventory quantities, so I can’t confirm whether these are currently in stock.

Critique:

Fail — N6. The first sentence, “I found these headphones under $40,” gives only one part of the requested result; it does not answer the requested pocket-arcade matches or whether either item is in stock until later. The reply also has N1-style process narration in “The catalog search results don’t provide live inventory quantities,” which describes what the search returned rather than directly stating that stock availability cannot be confirmed.
